description: Generate a Walkthrough for one code change or a stack. The Walkthrough worker runs this skill; people start it from the dashboard.
A Walkthrough helps a reviewer who has no context understand a code change
without reading all of its code. The story leads. Code is the evidence.
The instruction gives the repository, the code changes (bottom first, with
base and head commits), and sometimes a source Conversation ID: the
Conversation that opened the code change.
If `submitWalkthrough` is not in your tools, this Turn is not a Walkthrough
generation. Say that Walkthroughs start from the dashboard, and stop.
1. Read the diff of each code change at the given commits. Use `gh pr diff`
or a shallow clone and `git diff BASE...HEAD`. Read callers or other
unchanged code when the change affects them.
2. If there is a source Conversation ID, read it to learn the intent. Start
with the most recent messages and go back only as far as you need. If you
cannot read it, continue with the code changes alone.
3. Pick the change type of each part. Each type has fixed slots, in this
reading order. Fill the slots that apply; do not invent structure.
4. Call `submitWalkthrough`. If it reports problems, fix all of them and call
it again. When it succeeds, reply with one short sentence and stop.

content.title: Walkthroughs: guided, citation-checked stories of a PR stack
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs: an experimental API that runs a hidden Turn to write a guided story of a PR stack, with every citation re-checked by Junior.

chapters.label: Starting a Walkthrough
chapters.caption: A signed-in person posts one PR to a new experimental API, and Junior starts one generation for its whole stack.
chapters.body: Behind the new `walkthroughs` experiment, a signed-in person posts a provider, repository, and PR number [1]. startWalkthrough stops unless a plugin can read that provider [4], reads the whole stack, and claims a version row for it [2]. Only the request that claimed the row creates the hidden Conversation, whose first message invokes the walkthrough skill; if that fails, the version is marked failed [3].

decisions.claim: Any signed-in viewer may walk through any repository that the GitHub plugin can read.
decisions.concern: Neither route checks the viewer's access to the repository, so a private diff could reach someone who cannot see it on GitHub.

asks: What happens when two people click at the same time?
Which instruction does the hidden Conversation receive?

chapters.label: Reading the stack
chapters.caption: Plugins gain read-only code change hooks, and GitHub finds the stack through the Stacks API or by walking base branches.
chapters.body: Core never calls GitHub: it calls the `codeChanges` hooks of the plugin named by the provider [1], as a system Actor that never asks anyone to sign in [2]. GitHub reads the requested PR, asks the Stacks API, and falls back to walking base branches down to trunk and up to the top, stopping where the chain forks [4][5]. Merged or closed layers drop out, except the requested one [3]. Diffs compare exact base and head SHAs, so a push during generation cannot change the story [6].

decisions.claim: The Stacks API returns 404 for every repository that cannot use stacks.
decisions.concern: Any other error makes readStack throw instead of falling back to the base-branch walk.

asks: Whose GitHub credentials do these reads use?

chapters.label: One version per snapshot
chapters.caption: A new table keeps one live version per stack at its commits, so repeat clicks join the running or ready generation.
chapters.body: A new `junior_walkthrough_versions` table records each generation; the document itself is JSON in attachment storage [1][5]. The snapshot key hashes every layer's number with its base and head SHAs [3]. A partial unique index allows one row per key that has not failed, so a conflicting insert returns the live version instead of starting a second run [2][4]. Completion only changes a row that is still generating [5]. The migration only adds a table and its indexes.
asks: Does a new push reuse the old version?
Why does nothing set parent_version_id yet?

chapters.label: Hidden generation Conversations
chapters.caption: Generation Conversations are public roots, but every Conversation list now leaves out the ones that a version row names.
chapters.body: A generation Conversation is an ordinary public root, so `listedConversation` now leaves out any Conversation that a version row names, using the unique index on that column [1]. The row claims the Conversation id before the Conversation exists, which is why there is no foreign key [2]. Intent comes from a source Conversation found through the marker that Junior writes in PR footers, and only a public one is used [3].

decisions.claim: Every Conversation list and search now runs a NOT EXISTS lookup against Walkthrough versions.
decisions.concern: A list that does not use listedConversation would still show generation Conversations.

decisions.claim: Ignoring a private source Conversation is better than giving the Walkthrough its intent.
decisions.concern: PRs opened from private threads get Walkthroughs with no intent from their Conversation.

chapters.label: The generation Turn
chapters.caption: The Turn worker spots a generation Conversation and runs it with the submit tool, no way to reach people, and tight limits.
chapters.body: Before each Turn, the worker asks whether the Conversation is generating a version and puts it on the run [1][2]. turnBehavior then returns WALKTHROUGH_GENERATION, a temporary flag until a `walkthrough` kind exists: no agents, review desk, subscriptions, or noReply [3], and only then is `submitWalkthrough` created [6]. Nobody watches these Turns, so they get 80 tool calls and $5 instead of the app defaults [4][5].

decisions.claim: 80 tool calls and $5 are enough for a Walkthrough of a ten-layer stack.
decisions.concern: A large stack that hits either cap ends without a document, and its version fails.

asks: Can a generation Turn message people or start agents?

chapters.label: What the model writes
chapters.caption: The model submits structured chapters that cite code by line range and never copy code or text.
chapters.body: The model writes only a WalkthroughOutput; Junior adds layers, excerpts, message text, and cost [1]. Each change type has fixed slots in reading order, so every bug fix reads the same way, and the skill lists them [2][5]. Evidence is a line range at a commit, a message seq, a link, or a check id [3]. Every file that is not mechanical must be cited or listed in `not_covered`, which #3124 renamed from camelCase [4].
asks: Where does the code a reader sees come from?

chapters.label: Every citation is re-checked
chapters.caption: submitWalkthrough re-reads diffs, files, and messages from their sources and rejects output with any citation that does not resolve or is missing.
chapters.body: submitWalkthrough does not trust the sandbox: it re-reads each layer's diff, the cited head files, and the cited messages, then validates [5]. Lockfiles, generated files, renames, and whitespace-only edits are dropped first, so nothing cites them [1]. A range must sit inside one hunk or a file at the head commit [2], every hunk must be cited or excused [3], and the prose must cite every evidence item [4]. Only then does Junior copy the cited lines into excerpts [6].

decisions.claim: Check evidence cannot pass yet, because the submit tool knows no check ids.
decisions.concern: The schema and skill offer checks, so a model that cites CI spends retries on a citation that always fails.

asks: Can the model put made-up code into the document?

chapters.label: Storing and serving
chapters.caption: A passing submission stores the document, and the read route checks source access again on every read.
chapters.body: A passing submission builds the document and completes the version; if the version stopped generating, the tool throws [1]. GET /api/walkthroughs/:id returns the status, the layers without their PR bodies, the cost so far from the generation Conversation's metrics, and the document once it is ready [2][4][5][6]. A document quotes its source Conversation, which can turn private later, so every read checks again that the viewer can see it [3].

chapters.label: Failure and retry
chapters.caption: A Turn that ends without a Walkthrough fails its version, and a generation stuck for 30 minutes is reclaimed on the next click.
chapters.body: After the agent returns, the worker calls finish(), which fails the version only if submit never completed it [1][2][5]. Before inserting, startWalkthroughVersion fails any row of the same snapshot that is still generating after 30 minutes [3][4]. A crashed run cannot hold the key, and the partial index lets the retry insert a fresh row.

decisions.claim: A run that throws on its final attempt can leave its version generating until the 30-minute reclaim.
decisions.concern: finish() runs only in the completion callback, so the page can show generating for up to 30 minutes, and no test covers the reclaim.

asks: Does finish() undo a Walkthrough that was already stored?

chapters.label: Tests and watch items
chapters.caption: Unit and integration tests cover validation, stack reads, versioning, the submit tool, and the HTTP flow.
chapters.body: Unit tests pin the validator's rules [1], and GitHub tests show the base-branch walk stopping at a fork [2]. Integration tests show that a second click joins the live version and a failed one does not block a retry [3]. They also show that the submit tool exists only in generation Turns and rejects citations that do not resolve [4], and that the HTTP flow queues one hidden Turn per snapshot and fails a Turn that ends without a document [5][6]. After shipping, watch versions stuck in generating and cost per stack.
